beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or from a secret store at runtime; never hard-code or commit the URI/primary key to source control or logs.
Keep a single long-lived MongoClient (or equivalent) per process and reuse it across requests; configure maxPoolSize/minPoolSize instead of creating a client per request.
Enable TLS/SSL on the MongoDB connection (tls=true / ssl=true) and validate server certificates; never disable certificate verification in production.
Store provider API keys (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY, DocumentDB keys) in Azure Key Vault or environment variables and reference them at runtime; rotate keys periodically and avoid printing them to logs.
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors and explicitly handle HTTP 429 / RequestRateTooLarge responses by reading the Retry-After header and delaying before retrying.

Use structured filters to narrow candidate documents before running vector similarity: first filter by specialty / language / insurance (indexed fields), then run vector search within that filtered subset (hybrid filter+vector query).
Create Mongo-style indexes on all fields used in equality or range filters (e.g., specialty, languages, acceptedInsurance) and create compound indexes if queries commonly combine those fields.

Create a vector index on the embedding field with a fixed numberOfDimensions matching the embedding model (e.g., 1536 for OpenAI text-embedding-3-large) and set the index's metric/similarity (cosine, dot, or euclidean) to match how embeddings are compared.

When creating an HNSW vector index tune key parameters (M/connectivity and efConstruction) for acceptable index build time vs search quality, and set efRuntime (efSearch/topK) at query time to control recall and performance.

Store embeddings as a fixed-length array of floats (consistent numeric type) in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding: [float,...]); avoid storing duplicate full embeddings in multiple fields and exclude embeddings from default projections when returning documents.

When responding to API calls, project out the embedding vector (exclude it) and only return the metadata (name, specialty, languages, acceptedInsurance, score) to reduce network and client processing costs.

Keep embedding dimensions and the embedding model consistent across all documents; include metadata that records which embedding model/version generated the vector so you can re-index if the model changes.
Make index and collection creation idempotent: check for existing index definitions before creating or use create-if-not-exists patterns so seeding scripts can be re-run safely.
Use pagination and a topK limit for vector queries (do not return unlimited hits); choose a modest default (e.g., topK=10) and allow callers to request fewer or more within safe bounds.

Monitor RU/s (provisioned throughput), request charge per query, index storage, and RU throttling metrics in Azure Portal/metrics; tune autoscale or RU allocation if vector/index operations cause high RU consumption.

Prefer autoscale (or appropriately provisioned RU/s) for workloads that include expensive vector searches or spikes (do not rely on minimal fixed throughput), and test expected QPS vs RU consumption in staging.
Respect and implement the platform’s rate-limiting behavior: back off on 429s, avoid tight retry loops, and add jitter to retry delays to prevent thundering-herd effects.

When using an external embedding provider (OpenAI), rate-limit and cache embedding requests, fallback to a deterministic embedding generator for offline tests, and never embed user secrets in the stored documents.

Exclude or redact PII not needed for search; store only the attributes required (specialty, languages, insurance, short bio), and ensure any patient-identifiable data is not stored in provider documents.

Write unit and integration tests that are idempotent against the shared database: seed known test documents, verify indexes and queries, and clean up or use a dedicated test collection/database to avoid interfering with production data.

Tune HNSW/IVF/DiskANN engine-specific parameters only after measuring: start with conservative efRuntime/topK, and increase efRuntime to improve recall if necessary; document the parameter values you used so the index can be rebuilt reproducibly.
Avoid multi-document transactions for common read-heavy vector search paths; prefer single-document atomic operations for upserts and use optimistic concurrency where necessary.

Project and store searchable text fields (bio, specialties) in normalized forms useful for filters (lowercase, canonicalized language tags) so equality/index lookups are reliable and language matching is consistent.

Limit the size of individual documents (keep documents reasonably small) because large embedded vectors and metadata increase RU costs and latency; if necessary, store large text externally and reference it.

When possible prefer provider-managed secrets (Managed Identity / Azure AD) over static keys for access to Azure resources; if using the MongoDB wire protocol and static keys are required, wrap them in Key Vault and rotate regularly.
